still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and branded oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.
Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro) has no US generic, retatrutide still lists at $1,299 behind commercial prior authorisation, and no incretin implant is on the market.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 30.5 ever − 21.1 current = 9.4 pts used-and-off; ~55% of current users are on ≥2nd course (11.6 pts) + ~2.2 pts cycled and off again = 13.8 pts ÷ 30.5 ≈ 45% cycled; remaining 7.2 pts stopped once and never restarted — consistent with ~one-third one-year persistence and restart rates nudged up (~45–50% within a year) by $39–69 generics. Age check: 0.20×11 + 0.33×19.8 + 0.24×30 + 0.23×22.5 ≈ 21.1. Users ≈ 21.1% × ~270M adults ≈ 57M. Payer mix (FICTIONAL): Medicare ~15M (26%: ~10.5M through diabetes/CV/CKD/OSA/dementia codes, ~4.5M through the new 2032 generic-first obesity benefit); Medicaid ~7M (12%; 24 states took the new optional obesity benefit); commercial ~13.5M (24%); legitimate cash ~15.5M (27%, now mostly generic semaglutide at $39–69); imported/counterfeit ~6M (10.5%). Public programmes are the largest payer at 38%. The bottom income third rose fastest (12 → 18) through Medicaid and the $39 floor; the top–bottom gap narrowed for the first time. Off-drug: ~25M adults have used and stopped, of whom ~5M are regainers over 50. Among adults with obesity (~33%), roughly 18% of all adults have never used a drug. Some of them cannot reach a prescriber or live in non-adopting Medicaid states, but a growing share say they refuse by choice. Pediatric: ~1.3% of under-18s (~2.7% of 12–17s). Under-12 use rose to ~0.3% of 6–11s on generic liraglutide via Medicaid EPSDT, then flattened after seven states limited under-12 prescribing to pediatric endocrinologists. Households with at least one user: ~38%.

access.public_coverage: Medicare Part D now covers obesity treatment under the July 2031 Medicare and Medicaid Obesity Treatment Access provisions, effective Jan 2032. Patients must use generic semaglutide first. Branded drugs require documented failure or a qualifying code, and continuing past 12 months requires ≥5% loss or maintenance. FICTIONAL 2032 annualised Part D incretin spend: coded users on generics 3.5M × $40 × 12 ≈ $1.7B; coded users on brands 7M × ~$235 × 12 ≈ $19.7B (dementia route ~2.6M × $255 × 12 ≈ $8.0B of that, after the 2031 extension to 60+ without CVD); obesity-benefit users 4.5M × ~$42 × 12 ≈ $2.3B. Total ≈ $23.7B, down from ~$29.7B in 2030 with ~50% more users. CBO scored the benefit at ~$27B net over 2032–41 (≈6M eventual users × $45 × 12 ≈ $3.2B/yr gross × 10 ≈ $32B, less ~$5B in scored offsets), against the ~$41B branded-era score. Medicaid: the optional obesity benefit carries an enhanced federal match and has been adopted by 24 states. ~5.5M users on generics × $32 × 12 ≈ $2.1B plus ~1.5M on brands × $210 × 12 ≈ $3.8B ≈ $5.9B gross. TRICARE covers generic semaglutide.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $4–30 a month across 100+ brands. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue products are sold widely outside patent-protected markets. Canadian generics cost CAD 40–70. Most global incretin volume is now generic semaglutide.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Semaglutide's US compound patent expired in Dec 2031. Five ANDA generics (Viatris, Teva, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's, Hikma) plus a Novo authorised generic launched in pens and vials. By mid-2032 cash prices run $39 (Cost Plus, Costco) to $69 (chain pharmacy), and Medicare/Medicaid net is ~$30–45. Employer coverage rose from 36% to 43%, almost entirely as generic-only tiers. Metabolic tracks shrank to ~3.6M enrollees (inside the 13.5M commercial users) because generics made verification less worth paying for. Brands persist where generics don't reach: tirzepatide on TrumpRx at $249–329, retatrutide $1,299 list, MariTide ~$279 direct, Wegovy pill starting doses $149. Tirzepatide+bimagrumab (Mar 2032) lists at ~$1,450 a month for the antibody, on a handful of commercial formularies and pending a Part B coverage decision. Access is now a floor question. $39 plus needles, a prescriber visit and a pharmacy within reach is the barrier, along with living in one of the 26 states that did not adopt the Medicaid option. Gray market ~6M, up from 5.2M despite cheap legal product. It runs on $10 'generic' vials from unlicensed online pharmacies, counterfeit generic pens (generic packaging is easier to fake than serialised brand pens), knockoff tirzepatide and retatrutide, and 'muscle stacks' sold as bimagrumab. Orals ~38% of users, down from 45% as cheap injectables took share.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic, and generic semaglutide since Dec 2031)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)
Activin type II receptor antibody, monthly IV infusion, as add-on to tirzepatide (bimagrumab; approved Mar 2032)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill; Rybelsus)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin; approved Oct 2031)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and CVD, extended Jun 2031 to adults 60+ with obesity without CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Jan 2032; ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines endorse GLP-1 agonists as second-line after naltrexone/acamprosate)
preservation of lean mass during incretin-induced weight loss (bimagrumab add-on to tirzepatide, adults with BMI ≥30, Mar 2032)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: generic injectable semaglutide for alcohol reduction (cheaper than the approved branded oral)
dementia-prevention use by 50–59-year-olds outside the label, cash-paid
microdosing generic semaglutide for 'steadiness', now discouraged by clinics after anhedonia labelling
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label, restricted in seven states)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Amycretin (filed Oct 2029) approved Oct 2031 at ~22% loss with nausea comparable to the weekly drugs. The muscle-preserving-combo driver is realised by bimagrumab (phase 3 with no filing stated at step start). Lilly filed in Jan 2031 and the FDA approved it in Mar 2032, 14 months later, as a monthly IV add-on to tirzepatide. On the label, lean-mass loss is cut by roughly half on DXA at similar fat loss. There are no fracture or function endpoints, a postmarketing fracture outcome trial is required, and labelled effects include muscle spasm, diarrhoea and acne. Marketing calls it 'weight loss without the frailty'. Oral semaglutide AUD phase 3 read out Feb 2031 with heavy-drinking days down ~30% vs placebo. The sNDA was filed May 2031 and approved Jan 2032 under priority review. Generic semaglutide is the only new generic incretin. Tirzepatide patents run to the mid-2030s. No implant exists; programmes remain phase 1. No oral matches tirzepatide. US net incretin revenue fell ~15% in 2032 on semaglutide genericisation while volume rose ~20%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Generic-era dosing errors (vial-to-pen conversions, skipped titration by cash users) drove a rise in ER visits for vomiting and dehydration in 2032.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained. FDA requires uniform concentration labelling across generic vials.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now centres on exocrine insufficiency.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after >2 years and ~1.45 after 3+ cycles. The 2031 dementia-label extension and the Medicare obesity benefit added ~5M older users, so absolute fracture counts are rising even though the per-user rate is unchanged. Bimagrumab halves DXA lean-mass loss, but nobody knows whether that prevents fractures.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. Bimagrumab carries a postmarketing fracture-outcome requirement. Medicare benefit pays for a baseline DXA in users 65+.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low; unchanged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA pooled 19 randomised trials that had used validated hedonic scales (SHAPS). Clinically meaningful anhedonia was ~2.1% on drug vs ~1.4% on placebo at 68 weeks, ~1.2% excess on retatrutide. The observational 7–8% vs 3% excess is now read as largely confounded (prior depression, stopping-related mood change), but critics note the trials excluded psychiatric history. The excess is real, dose-related and uncommon.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling (May 2031) lists 'anhedonia/emotional blunting' as an uncommon adverse reaction (≥1/1,000 to <1/100) with advice to reassess dose. Postmarketing observational study continues.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Cheap generics made restarting easier, so cycling is up slightly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. It underpins the Medicare 12-month continuation rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron, vitamin D and fat-soluble vitamin deficiency documented in low-intake and long-term users; unchanged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label language on annual micronutrient monitoring added Mar 2031.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Unchanged at ~4.1 vs ~1.9 per 1,000 person-years after 5+ years on semaglutide. A small Danish follow-up suggests partial recovery of faecal elastase within a year of stopping. Tirzepatide exposure past 5 years is still too thin for a rate. No new signal in the window.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide labels (brand and generic) added a warning and faecal elastase testing advice in Jul 2031. Class-wide labelling deferred pending tirzepatide data. EMA PRAC concluded with a similar warning.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Nine years of semaglutide follow-up and no further long-horizon finding beyond EPI. First pediatric (6–11) bone and growth interim report due 2033.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue. Seven states restrict under-12 prescribing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Non-approved-product adverse-event reports passed ~23,000 by mid-2032, and poison-centre calls are ~6× 2025. In May 2032 CDC linked 64 bloodstream infections (3 deaths) in 11 states to endotoxin- and Burkholderia-contaminated 'generic semaglutide' vials sold by an unlicensed Telegram-advertised pharmacy. Counterfeits of the new generic pens and 'bimagrumab' muscle stacks are the fastest-growing categories.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CBP seizures roughly tripled from 2030. FDA added generic-semaglutide-labelled imports to the import alert and opened a pharmacy verification lookup. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak. Seven states now license incretin telehealth prescribers.

food_and_beverage.state: About 38% of households have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~11% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. The new decline is in lower-income zip codes: Medicaid and $39 generics reached the value-pack shopper, and Dollar General reports private-label snack volume down mid-single digits in 2032. Protein-fortified lines are migrating to value price points. Bakeries and 'whole food' grocers in unmedicated-movement strongholds (Tulsa, Tyler TX, northwest Arkansas) report growth.

alcohol.state: Spirits volumes are down ~14% from 2025 and beer ~9%. The AUD label and guideline endorsement moved heavy drinkers, a disproportionate share of volume, into treatment through VA, Medicaid and EAPs. Brown-Forman cut a Kentucky distillery shift. Midwestern bar closures continue. Non-alcoholic lines keep growing but stay below 6% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic flat to slightly down. Smaller checks spread from casual dining into lower-income QSRs as uptake reached them. Protein bowls are standard. Unmedicated 'full table' supper clubs and family-style Southern restaurants are a small growing niche.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. A small 'soft' fashion line (loose linen, aprons, generous cuts) sells as unmedicated-movement aesthetic through Etsy-scale makers and one Target capsule.

fitness.state: Strength and DXA keep growing, but premium clubs face a new pitch: bimagrumab promises the muscle without the coaching, and clubs answer with 'function, not just mass' testing. Budget gyms in Medicare-heavy suburbs add 'SilverSneakers strength' classes tied to the benefit's DXA. Employer metabolic tracks are shrinking.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% in 2032 as semaglutide went generic. Employers re-added generic-only weight tiers (coverage up to 43%) and kept brands behind prior authorisation. Part D premiums stabilised because the generic-first rule offset new users. Adherence-tied wellness differentials persist but are being marketed less.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell sharply on generic entry, with Danish job cuts in Bagsværd and Kalundborg. It leans on the oral, the AUD label and amycretin. Lilly grows on tirzepatide's dementia label, retatrutide and bimagrumab. US generic makers (Viatris, Teva, Sandoz) run low-margin, high-volume businesses. Anti-counterfeit costs rose again.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: With semaglutide at $39, a lean body no longer signals much money. What signals money is composition and the brand. A lifted, scanned body on tirzepatide plus bimagrumab reads as the top tier. A thin, soft body reads as generic or Medicaid. A deliberately full body, with visible appetite and a movement pin, now reads as a choice instead of a lack, and that is new.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class marker moved from thin to muscle to muscle you didn't have to work for: Charlotte and Austin professionals post bimagrumab infusion selfies the way they once posted DXA printouts. In Toledo and Dayton the newly covered over-65s are thinner than their children. Bottom-third women 50–64 who had regained are going back on through Medicaid in adopting states, and stay regained in the 26 that did not.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals keep getting shorter among users. The counter-ritual hardened into the 'full table': long Sunday suppers with bread, gravy and pie, organised by Bread Alone congregations (~900 now) and secular Unmedicated chapters. They are strongest in Tulsa and northwest Arkansas, among evangelical women 25–45. School lunch fights moved to state legislatures.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added an 'Unmedicated' badge alongside 'on' and 'lean-mass verified', and it is the fastest-growing filter among users under 30 in the South. Alcohol-free first dates are common among AUD-indicated users. Mismatch complaints persist, but clinics now screen for blunting and adjust doses instead of telling couples to wait it out.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Once the drug cost $39, declining it stopped being a sign of poverty and became an identity. The Unmedicated movement has its own aesthetics (flour, softness, handwritten recipe cards, the hollow-circle 'U' pin) and its own politics, which run from MAHA state legislators to Unmuted's working-class off-nights in Detroit. For users, appetite is still noise to be managed. For the movement, keeping your appetite is the point.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Labelled since May 2031 as an uncommon adverse reaction. Pooled RCT excess is ~0.7 points of clinically meaningful anhedonia, ~1.2 on retatrutide. The observational 7–8% figure is now widely cited as an overestimate, though Unmuted disputes that. Mild 'evenness' is still commonly reported, and clinicians no longer treat it as a selling point.
interior_life.framing: A side effect: uncommon, dose-related, something to screen for. HR has mostly dropped 'steadiness'. Unmuted says the label shrank the number without changing the experience, and the industry says the label proves the scare was overblown.
interior_life.effect_on_work: After the label change, employment counsel warned that promoting a drug for an effect now listed as a psychiatric adverse reaction invites ADA claims. A national call-centre operator settled one of the two EEOC charges in Nov 2031, removed 'even under pressure' from shift-lead competencies and paid $2.1M. Metabolic tracks (~3.6M) still verify adherence for premium differentials, but their materials now talk about cardiometabolic cost, not temperament. Columbus-corridor plant clinics still give monthly shots and now ask a two-question hedonic screen at each visit.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'flat' fiction imprint was rebranded. Unmuted off-nights merged into the wider Unmedicated scene: loud food, live gospel and punk bills in Detroit and Baltimore, and supper-club concerts in Tulsa. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in insured suburbs. Bar trivia nights are moving to cafés.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Therapists report fewer 'parallel lives' cases framed as drug effects and more framed as mismatched identities, with one partner on and one partner unmedicated. AUD-indicated use changed drinking couples more than any weight indication did. Some spouses describe sobriety they didn't choose for themselves.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The unmedicated movement won where it aimed at children and advertising, not premiums. Seven states passed under-12 limits and incretin ad bans, but none followed Illinois on adherence-conditioned premiums. The 'sedated electorate' claim faded with the label number. The live divide is now among older voters: Medicare users who gained a benefit versus movement voters who call it a pharma subsidy.

state.regulatory_posture: The FDA moved fast on generics (five ANDAs at patent expiry), amycretin, the AUD label and bimagrumab, and labelled anhedonia as uncommon. The restrictive turn is at state level. Texas, Florida, Tennessee, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Ohio and Utah enacted laws from late 2031 to mid-2032 that limit under-12 incretin prescribing to board-certified pediatric endocrinologists, ban incretin advertising on social media and influencer platforms, and cap telehealth-only initial prescriptions at 90 days before an in-person visit. A Florida ad-ban challenge on First Amendment grounds is pending in the 11th Circuit.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The July 2031 federal law created Part D obesity coverage (generic-first, 12-month continuation rule) and an optional Medicaid obesity benefit with enhanced match, adopted by 24 states. TrumpRx continues for brands. No mandate to take the drugs exists anywhere.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Medicare's continuation rule needs weight data at 12 months, recorded by prescribers. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Employer verification persists under the 2027 guidance, but the shrinking tracks mean fewer workers are covered by it. Clinic administration records for monthly drugs still flow to wellness vendors under consent forms.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT ruled in Apr 2032 that CDL holders may take incretins for AUD with medical-examiner clearance and a 30-day observation period. TRICARE covers generic semaglutide for obesity. The Army recruit pilot expanded to two more training centres using generics.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Generic semaglutide removed most of the US–Denmark price fight, and the argument is now with India over mail-order. CBP seizures tripled, US–India talks added a pharmacy-licensing annex that remains unsigned, and Novo's Danish job cuts became a domestic political issue in Copenhagen.

events.event: FDA adds 'anhedonia/emotional blunting' to incretin class labels as an uncommon adverse reaction after pooled analysis of 19 trials finds a placebo-adjusted excess under one percentage point; employers quietly retire 'steadiness' language

Congress, citing a CBO rescore of ~$27B over ten years in a generics era, creates generic-first Medicare Part D obesity coverage and an optional Medicaid benefit with enhanced match, both effective January 2032
Semaglutide's compound patent expires; five ANDA generics and a Novo authorised generic launch, and by mid-2032 a month's supply sells for $39 at Cost Plus and Costco and $69 at chain pharmacies
FDA approves oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder on priority review; ASAM and VA/DoD guidelines endorse GLP-1 agonists as second-line AUD therapy within weeks

FDA approves Lilly's bimagrumab as a monthly infused add-on to tirzepatide that halves lean-mass loss on DXA, with a required fracture-outcome trial; Lilly's campaign promises 'weight loss without the frailty'

CDC ties 64 bloodstream infections and 3 deaths in 11 states to contaminated 'generic semaglutide' vials from an unlicensed online pharmacy; Texas, Florida, Ohio and four other states pass under-12 prescribing limits and social-media ad bans by summer
events.driver: market_shock: generic_flood_counterfeits; state_action: restriction; cultural_response: natural_movement

open_tensions: The Medicare benefit was scored on $40 generics, but the 2031 dementia extension and bimagrumab push older users toward brands costing $235–1,450. Whether Part D's generic-first rule holds against fracture-risk and dementia arguments decides the next budget fight.

Legal semaglutide costs $39, yet ~6M people still buy gray-market product, including counterfeit generic pens that are easier to fake than serialised brands. State telehealth caps meant to curb the flood may push rural users toward unlicensed shops.

Bimagrumab is sold as solving 'skinny-frail' on DXA alone. The fracture trial won't report for years, while millions of new over-65 users build up exposure, the semaglutide EPI warning applies, and tirzepatide's long-term data are still thin.

With the drug cheap enough that refusing it is a choice, the unmedicated movement has become a political identity. Its wins so far are child and advertising restrictions, and its next targets are the Medicare benefit and school-based prescribing.

prose.headline: The $39 Shot: Generic semaglutide made Medicare the biggest payer, and turned saying no into an identity
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 about one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, roughly fifty-seven million people, and nearly a third have tried one. The biggest change is not the number but the price. In December 2031 semaglutide's patent ran out, and within six months a month's supply cost $39 at Costco and Cost Plus and $69 at a chain pharmacy. The $1,349 list price is still printed on the Wegovy box. It mostly measures how far the price has fallen.

Congress acted just before the price fell, once the price made the decision cheap. In July 2031 it wrote obesity into Medicare Part D on a generic-first basis and gave states an enhanced match to do the same in Medicaid. Twenty-four states did. Public programmes now pay for about two in five users, the largest share, and Medicare spends less on these drugs than it did in 2030 while covering half again as many people. The remaining barriers are a prescriber, a pharmacy, a box of needles, and whether your state took the Medicaid option. The bottom income third rose fastest. In Toledo and Dayton, retired cafeteria workers who regained everything after the old pilot ended are thin again on an $8 copay.

The brands moved up-market. Lilly's tirzepatide picked up a dementia-prevention label for over-60s without heart disease in 2031. In March its new monthly infusion, bimagrumab, won approval as an add-on that halves the muscle lost during weight loss, at least on a scanner. The advertising says frailty is solved. The fracture trial that would show whether it is will report in a few years. In Charlotte and Austin, infusion-chair selfies have replaced DXA printouts.

Novo's consolation was alcohol. In January its oral semaglutide was approved for alcohol use disorder, and the addiction societies endorsed the class as second-line treatment. VA clinics, Medicaid programmes and employer EAPs moved heavy drinkers onto it, and since heavy drinkers buy much of the liquor, spirits volumes are down about a seventh from 2025. The Transportation Department now lets truck drivers take it with a medical examiner's sign-off.

In May 2031 the FDA settled, as far as a label can, the argument over flatness. Pooled trial data put the drug's excess risk of clinically meaningful anhedonia below one percentage point, and the label now lists it as uncommon. Employers dropped the word 'steadiness' from their competency frameworks almost overnight, and one call-centre company settled its federal complaint. Clinics ask two screening questions at each visit. Critics say the trials excluded the people most at risk. Most people have stopped talking about it.

Cheap legal drugs have not emptied the gray market. About six million people still buy elsewhere: ten-dollar 'generic' vials advertised on Telegram, fake copies of the new generic pens, knockoff retatrutide, and muscle stacks sold as bimagrumab. In May the CDC traced sixty-four bloodstream infections and three deaths to contaminated vials from one unlicensed pharmacy. Poison-centre calls are six times what they were in 2025.

That outbreak gave a movement its legislation. When the drug cost hundreds of dollars, not taking it looked like being poor. At $39 it looks like a choice, and in Tulsa, northwest Arkansas and east Texas, refusing it has become an identity. Unmedicated chapters and Bread Alone congregations hold long Sunday suppers, members wear a hollow-circle pin, and dating apps offer an 'Unmedicated' badge. In seven states, legislators allied with the movement limited prescriptions for under-12s to pediatric endocrinologists and banned incretin ads on social media. They left the employer premium rules alone. Illinois is still the only state to ban them.

From a distance, the country is cheaper to treat, a little thinner, and drinking less. The people who refuse the drug now do so openly.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Kowalski, sixty-seven, gets to the Kroger pharmacy on Monroe Street before it opens and waits in her car with the heater on. The bag is ready: four generic pens, $8.40. Under the counter there's a laminated poster now, a photo of a vial with a red X through it. DO NOT BUY ONLINE. The pharmacist, Tran, taps it with her pen when she hands the bag over, the way she does with everyone.

At home Ray is at the table with his pill and his water, waiting out the thirty minutes. He hasn't opened a Busch Light since Easter. He says the TV is boring now. She says it was always boring.

She injects in the bathroom, the left side this week, and writes the date on the calendar on the fridge. Under it is the DXA appointment the plan paid for. The card says her hips are 'osteopenic, monitor.'

At four she drives to Kayla's in Perrysburg for Sunday-on-Monday, because Kayla's church does the full table on Mondays now. There are eleven people, three loaves, gravy in the good boat. Kayla wears the little white circle pin on her apron. Nobody says anything about Denise's plate, which is half a roll and some chicken. Liam, nine, takes thirds of pie, and his mother watches him do it like it's a prayer.

In the car Denise eats the other half of the roll. She isn't hungry for it. She just wanted to see whether she'd like it.

She liked it all right. She sets the crust on the dashboard for the birds.
